profile.label: r2-walk-input-stall-profile-v2

gpuContextEvidence.inference: The handler created after chooser/start and active throughout the private canvas visit owns the long flush; the earlier original-designer handler has zero commands after ready. These lifecycle timings and the two canvas snapshots support private Walk ownership. No explicit DOM-canvas-to-handler or route-id-to-handler binding is present in the trace.
gpuContextEvidence.commandLimit: put_offset identifies command-buffer positions, not GL opcodes. The long flush starts before the failing input and during the preceding short Walk tick, so it processes earlier client commands. The exact call, shader, texture, driver operation or GPU scheduling mechanism cannot be recovered from this trace.

findings: The reproduced444.9ms input delay is mostly post-handler and438.413ms of the sampled interval is renderer-main idle.

A 495.856ms CrGpuMain task overlaps the delay; its nested WebGL/CommandBuffer flush is 495.814/495.812ms wall time but about 1.2ms thread CPU. This is a GPU/driver-side wait or scheduling stall signature, not a 444.9ms JavaScript loop.
No renderer-main RunTask>=50ms overlaps the input delay. Current script mapping identifies the short render stack as the private Walk tick calling the existing ThreeStage beginWalk render method.

Original designer frames remain3 and paused throughout chooser/ready/complete snapshots. Its visible dataset remains first-picture. This proves no original completed renders during the sampled phases; it cannot establish that every background compile/detail timer was cancelled.

The 495.807ms PutChanged batch names handler .WebGL-0x3224048cbc00 on current GL context 0x5. It begins at 17972.719ms, before input at 18030.900000095367ms, during the prior Walk tick at 17969.399–17972.900ms. Earlier batches on that handler end at offsets 7369, 13640 and 20269; this one ends at 22799. Offsets do not identify individual GL commands.

Exactly two WebGL handlers occur. The earlier handler has no commands after ready; the later handler first appears after private stage creation and remains active throughout the visit. This supports private Walk ownership by lifecycle inference, without a direct DOM-canvas/route-id binding. Shader compilation, texture upload or a particular driver operation remains unproven.
